title: Code review report: T-003 Package A (T-003a app shell, build and branding; T-003b operative sign-in, secure session and sign-out)
summary: Round 1 for Package A (ac3ba7f): CHANGES REQUESTED, with 2 blockers, 3 majors and 9 minors. The backend session work is sound. Only SHA-256 of a 256-bit secret is stored. Lookup is by primary key, then hmac.compare_digest, under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. Rotation, the 60 s grace window (measured from the original rotation, so it cannot be stretched) and reuse revocation follow design section 4. Idle expiry is capped at the absolute expiry. Every request with a sid token checks the session by primary key, so sign-out and deactivation take effect at once, and web tokens behave as before. Migration 0009 matches design section 7 and gets app-role DML without TRUNCATE. Nothing logs a token, password or email (tested). T-003a is complete: config validation, branding snapshot, reachability gate, one React copy (verified: one node_modules/react 19.3.0, and RN 0.88.1's renderer embeds 19.3.0), allowBackup false, cleartext only for development, and the CI mobile job. BLOCKER 1: the mobile half of T-003b is not in the commit (no SessionManager, SecureTokenStore, sign-in screen, Stack.Protected guard, sign-out dialog or account_inactive screen, and none of the RNTL or Jest tests for scenarios 1 to 12), yet the commit message and PENDING_TICKETS treat T-003b as done. BLOCKER 2: the new mobile tooling brings glob 13.0.7 and 10.5.0 (GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4, moderate) and deepmerge 4.3.1 (GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4, low, no fixed release). Both are build and test tools only, not in the app bundle, so the blocker clears with an override or a recorded deferral. MAJOR: the shared refresh hook deadlocks if the refresh handler itself goes through callApi and gets a 401 (reproduced: the call never settles); onUnauthorized runs once per concurrent caller, not once (reproduced: 3 calls for 3 concurrent 401s), which breaks a spec'd test note; and the WAF rate rule for POST /api/v1/auth/sessions (T-003b INFRA delta) is missing. The reviewer ran npm audit, npm ls, mobile eslint and two scratch Vitest probes; the backend suite was not re-run. Reported results at HEAD: backend 1860, shared 453, web 300, mobile 29, e2e 149, all green.

blocks.heading: Round 1 (2 BLOCKER, 3 MAJOR, 9 MINOR)
rows: BLOCKER

T-003b mobile half missing (specs/T-003b.md 'Mobile' and test notes for scenarios 1 to 12). Absent: mobile/src/api/sessionManager.ts, SecureTokenStore (expo-secure-store is not even a dependency), the sign-in screen (mobile/app/sign-in.tsx renders SignInPlaceholder 'coming soon'), Stack.Protected for (app), the sign-out dialog with the unsent count, the account_inactive screen, the device_id in SecureStore, the proactive refresh, and every RNTL or Jest test listed for scenarios 1 to 12. The commit message says T-003b is delivered and backend/tests/contract.py removed T-003b from PENDING_TICKETS. Owner: mobile

Open. Build the T-003b mobile part as specified, with its tests, before T-003b is marked done. If the orchestrator meant to land only the backend and shared part (work-packages allow backend first), record that split in specs/T-003b.md and the progress page and keep T-003b open. Then this item becomes the next step, not a blocker on this commit
BLOCKER

Known vulnerabilities in packages the diff adds (mobile tooling): glob 13.0.7 (via @expo/cli, @expo/fingerprint, @jest/reporters) and glob 10.5.0 (via test-exclude, jest-expo), GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4 (moderate, fixed in 14.0.2); deepmerge 4.3.1 (via jest-config), GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 (low, no fixed release). npm audit: 23 (1 low, 22 moderate), none before this commit. All are build and test time only and absent from the Android bundle. Owner: architect

Open. Either add a root override glob ^14.0.2 (precedent: the minimatch override, ARCHITECTURE line 552) and prove jest coverage, expo export and expo-doctor still work, or record a deliberate deferral for both in ARCHITECTURE.md (tooling-only, no runtime path). deepmerge can only be deferred until a fixed release exists
MAJOR

shared/src/api/client.ts:73-104 refresh single flight deadlocks when the refresh handler uses callApi (the natural way to call refreshDeviceSession through the generated client). The refresh call's own 401 (session_ended) goes into attempt(), refreshOnce() returns the in-flight promise, and that promise is waiting for this same call. Reproduced in a scratch Vitest: the original call never settles. The sync engine and every screen would hang instead of reaching sign-in. Owner: web (shared)

Open. Give callApi an option to skip refresh (callApi(call, { refresh: false })) and use it for createDeviceSession, refreshDeviceSession and endDeviceSession, or never refresh for codes session_ended, account_inactive and invalid_credentials. Add a Vitest where refresh() calls callApi(refreshDeviceSession) that answers 401 session_ended, and assert the original call rejects promptly and onUnauthorized runs
MAJOR

shared/src/api/client.ts:103-104: when a shared refresh fails, every waiting caller runs unauthorizedHandler, so N concurrent 401s give N onUnauthorized calls. Reproduced: 3 calls for 3 concurrent 401s. specs/T-003b.md Shared requires 'refresh failure calls onUnauthorized once'. The added test covers a single caller only. On mobile, N calls means N sign-out and navigation actions. Owner: web (shared)

Open. Call onUnauthorized once per failed refresh: inside refreshOnce when the result is false, or guarded by the burst's promise. Add the spec'd Vitest: three concurrent 401s with a failing refresh give exactly one onUnauthorized call
MAJOR

T-003b INFRA delta not delivered: the WAF login rate rule still matches only POST /api/v1/auth/login (infra/terraform/modules/waf). POST /api/v1/auth/sessions is a second password-guessing endpoint with no rate limit, before T-003b's sign-in screen ships. Owner: infra

Open. Extend the rate-based rule's scope-down to POST /api/v1/auth/sessions, with the same percent-encoding-safe matching fixed in the INFRA-4/5 round. Refresh needs no rate rule: the 256-bit secret is not guessable
MINOR

backend/app/services/sessions.py:190: is_active is checked before the secret. With only a session id (no secret), anyone can learn that the account was deactivated (account_inactive versus session_ended). Line 210 also revokes a live session for any wrong secret, so a session id alone can sign a phone out. Session ids are in the JWT sid claim and in every session log line. Owner: backend

Open. Compare the hash (current, or previous within grace) first, then return account_inactive, then the revoked and expired checks. Scenario 11 still holds because the phone holds a valid token. Architect to confirm the revoke-on-any-mismatch rule (see questions)
MINOR

shared/src/api/client.ts:47-56: on React Native, fetch is whatwg-fetch, which rejects an abort with DOMException('Aborted','AbortError') and drops signal.reason (node_modules/whatwg-fetch/dist/fetch.umd.js:537,579). The fallback's TimeoutError reason never reaches networkError(), so a timeout on the phone is reported as network_error, not timeout. The Vitest stub rejects with signal.reason and so cannot catch this. Owner: web (shared)
Open. In timeoutFetch's catch, prefer signal.reason when signal.aborted (networkError(signal.aborted ? signal.reason : cause)). Add a test whose fetch stub rejects with a plain AbortError
MINOR

shared/src/api/client.ts:73-79: single flight covers only overlapping 401s. A request sent with the old token whose 401 arrives after the refresh settled starts a second refresh, so it is not 'once per burst'. Not a loop (retry is bounded), but it causes extra rotations, which matters with the grace rule. Owner: web (shared)
Open. Record the access token used for each attempt. On 401, if the token store already holds a different token, retry without refreshing
MINOR

shared/src/operative/semver.ts:10 differs from the contract SemVer (api/openapi.yaml:2023, ^[0-9]{1,4}\.[0-9]{1,4}\.[0-9]{1,4}$) and from backend/app/versioning.py. TS accepts -prerelease and +build and unlimited digits, rejects leading zeros, and trims. The server rejects '1.0.0-rc.1' as app_version with 422, while the client treats it as valid. Owner: web (shared)

Open. Use the contract pattern in the twin (no prerelease or build; 1 to 4 digits), or widen the contract and backend deliberately. Add a shared case table read by pytest and Vitest, as for validationCases.json
MINOR
backend/app/config.py:79-82: REFRESH_REUSE_GRACE_SECONDS has no upper bound (a mistaken 86400 would turn off reuse detection for a day) and DEVICE_ACCESS_TTL_SECONDS has none either. Owner: backend
Open. Add le=300 to the grace and le=3600 to the access TTL (or values the architect picks), with tests like test_access_token_ttl_has_a_floor
MINOR

web/Dockerfile:10: copying mobile/package.json makes the web build stage's npm ci install the whole Expo and React Native tree (about 990 extra packages, with their install scripts). The final nginx image is unchanged, but builds are slower and the build stage has a much larger supply-chain surface. Owner: web
Open. Run npm ci --workspace @jobproof/shared --workspace @jobproof/web --include-workspace-root, keeping the manifest copy so the lockfile validates. Confirm the image still builds
MINOR

.github/workflows/ci.yml:87,93,122: the web job's npm run lint and npm test now include mobile, so mobile lint and Jest (including the npx expo config test) run twice. expo-doctor runs through npx --yes outside the lockfile (version pinned, integrity not locked) and needs the Expo API, so it can fail CI on an outside outage. Owner: infra
Open. Limit the web job to -w @jobproof/shared -w @jobproof/web. Add expo-doctor as a mobile devDependency so the lockfile pins it, or mark that step continue-on-error with a visible warning
MINOR

Dependencies and config details: test-renderer pinned at 1.3.0 (1.3.1 is latest); eas.json cli.version '>= 18.0.0' with eas-cli unverified (design section 2); no splash configured, though specs/T-003a.md asks for a plain splash with the app name. Owner: architect (versions), mobile (splash)
Open. Bump or justify test-renderer, record the eas-cli version in ARCHITECTURE section 3, and add a splash placeholder in app.config.ts
MINOR

ARCHITECTURE.md drift: lines 11, 40, 60-62, 101, 116, 150, 162, 174, 259, 283-284 and 305 still mark T-003a and T-003b items planned. Line 101 says web React 19.3.1 (now 19.3.0, pinned by root overrides). Line 60's PENDING_TICKETS list and the gen:check note are stale. Owner: architect

blocks.heading: What the reviewer found sound
items: Token handling: refresh token '<uuid>.<43 chars>' from secrets.token_urlsafe(32); only SHA-256 stored (CHAR(64)); lookup by primary key, then hmac.compare_digest; no timing oracle on the hash.

Rotation: row lock (FOR UPDATE); current hash rotates and moves to previous; previous within grace rotates again without moving rotated_at (the window cannot be extended); anything else revokes with reuse_detected; expired or revoked sessions roll back with no change. Tests cover the grace, after the grace, two generations old, a wrong secret, a malformed token, and two concurrent refreshes.

Expiry: idle = min(now + idle days, absolute) at create and every refresh; refresh_expires_at reported; absolute expiry also enforced on access tokens in current_user; FIXED_NOW tests for 30-day idle, 90-day absolute and 15-minute access.

Revocation is immediate: current_user loads the session by primary key for sid tokens, so sign-out and deactivation act on the next request. A sid belonging to another user is unauthenticated. The role always comes from the database. Web tokens without sid keep today's behaviour and code.

Sign-in: the password is checked first (argon2 cost on every path), then 403 operatives_only with no row created; same device replaces the old session, with a retry on the unique-index race; endDeviceSession returns 204 for web tokens and repeats.
CLI deactivate-user: one transaction, idempotent, keeps the first revocation reason, prints the user id only.
Logging: session_id and outcome only. A test checks captured log records for both refresh secrets, access tokens, passwords and emails. The 422 handler never echoes input.

Migration 0009 matches design section 7 (checks, partial unique (user_id, device_id) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL, FK RESTRICT, user_id index); downgrade drops the table; round trip and constraint tests; app role gets SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE but no TRUNCATE (tested); seed truncates auth_sessions.
Config: MOBILE_MIN_VERSION_ANDROID semver-validated at startup; idle <= max days enforced; access TTL floor of 60.
GET /app/status: public, no database access (tested), Cache-Control no-store, server_time from app.clock, api_version tested equal to the contract version.

Shared: web passes no refresh, so its 401 path is byte-for-byte the old behaviour. The retry is bounded to one, so there is no infinite loop. The AbortSignal fallback clears its timer and listeners on settle (tested with the globals deleted). parseBrandingSnapshot moved unchanged and web delegates to it.

Mobile config: API_BASE_URL required and https unless APP_VARIANT=development, where cleartext is allowed only via expo-build-properties; allowBackup false; minSdk 29; blocked permissions list as design section 12; production package uk.co.jobproof.operative, with a suffix per variant; eas.json holds no URLs; the real npx expo config output is asserted in a test.
One React copy: root overrides plus exact pins; npm ls shows one react 19.3.0; the RN 0.88.1 ReactFabric renderer embeds '19.3.0'; singleReact.test.ts guards it.

Branding snapshot: validated (hex, length, control characters), corrupt snapshot removed, primary contrast re-checked before use, only server answers stored; scenarios 2, 3, 4 and 7 covered by RNTL; wording, URL-literal and deep-import scans in Jest plus an ESLint restriction.
CI mobile job: pinned actions, persist-credentials false, lint, Jest, expo-doctor and expo export with EXPO_OFFLINE.

blocks.heading: Questions for the architect
items: Was this commit meant to land only the backend and shared part of T-003b? If so, record the split in specs/T-003b.md and progress, and keep T-003b open (BLOCKER 1 then becomes the next step).

Reuse rule: should a correct session id with an unknown secret revoke the session (design: 'anything else'), given that session ids are logged and in the JWT? An alternative is to revoke only on a match with a known earlier hash, which would need a short hash history.

Two refreshes of the same token both succeed, and the first response's token dies at once (test_two_refreshes_at_once_do_not_fail). The SessionManager in T-003b and the background task in design 3.5 must share one refresh across the foreground app and the headless task, or the phone may keep the dead token and trip reuse_detected. Please state this in specs/T-003b.md.

Variant package ids (.dev, .preview, .screenshots): R10 pilots on preview builds, so pilot users install uk.co.jobproof.operative.preview, and moving them to production later is a separate app with separate local data. Intended?
